newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: About 10 detained over attack on Tajik president.
newsitem.headline: About 10 detained over attack on Tajik president.

text.p: About ten people have been detained by the authorities in Tajikistan in connection with last Wednesday's assassination attempt against the former Soviet republic's leader, presidential spokesman said on Saturday.
President Imomali Rakhmonov was injured on Wednesday when a hand grenade exploded near his car in the northern town of Khudjand on Wednesday.

Rakhmonov's spokesman Zafar Saidov gave no details of the latest string of arrests, but said some of the detained may be released on Sunday if investigators concluded they were not involved in the attack.
A man, who according to the officials carried out the attack in which two people were killed and tens inured, has been arrested by police soon after the blast.

Saidov said that Rakhmonov, who had been wounded in the legs and still has to undergo an operation to remove all the shrapnel from a leg wound, was well enough to chair a government session planned for Sunday.
Tajikistan, a remote mountain state which borders Afghanistan and China, is still reeling from a four-year civil war which has claimed the lives of tens of thousands. Armed bands roam the republic.
The government has condemned the attack as a "terrorist act" but has so far not blamed any one group for the assassination attempt.

Both Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, Rakhmonov's main foe in the civil war, and the National Revival of Tajikistan bloc, part of the republic's so-called "third" political force and based around Khudjand, have denied any involvement in the attack.
Diplomats and opposition sources say the attack could be a reaction to the government's violent crushing of a prison riot in Khudjand earlier this month, which left 20 dead.
The riot's leaders and Rakhmonov's would-be assassin were said by the authorities to have been involved in an anti-government demonstration in May last year.
